If this fails, 699 * pixd hasn't been changed. But we want to signal that the copy 700 * failed, so return NULL. This will cause a memory leak if the 701 * return ptr is assigned to pixd, but that is preferred to proceeding 702 * with an incorrect pixd, and in any event this use case of 703 * pixCopy() -- reallocating into an existing pix -- is infrequent. */ 704 if (pixResizeImageData(pixd, pixs) == 1) 705 return (PIX *)ERROR_PTR("reallocation of data failed", procName, NULL); 706 707 /* Copy non-image data fields */ 708 pixCopyColormap(pixd, pixs); 709 pixCopySpp(pixd, pixs); 710 pixCopyResolution(pixd, pixs); 711 pixCopyInputFormat(pixd, pixs); 712 pixCopyText(pixd, pixs); 713 714 /* Copy image data */ 715 memcpy(pixd->data, pixs->data, bytes); 716 return pixd; 717 } 718 719 720 /*! 721 * \brief pixResizeImageData() 722 * 723 * \param[in] pixd gets new uninitialized buffer for image data 724 * \param[in] pixs determines the size of the buffer; not changed 725 * \return 0 if OK, 1 on error 726 * 727 * 
   728   * Notes:
   729   *      (1) If the sizes of data in pixs and pixd are unequal, this
   730   *          frees the existing image data in pixd and allocates
   731   *          an uninitialized buffer that will hold the required amount
   732   *          of image data in pixs.  The image data from pixs is not
   733   *          copied into the new buffer.
   734   *      (2) On failure to allocate, pixd is unchanged.
   735   *
736 */ 737 l_ok 738 pixResizeImageData(PIX *pixd, 739 const PIX *pixs) 740 { 741 l_int32 w, h, d, wpl, bytes; 742 l_uint32 *data; 743 744 PROCNAME("pixResizeImageData"); 745 746 if (!pixs) 747 return ERROR_INT("pixs not defined", procName, 1); 748 if (!pixd) 749 return ERROR_INT("pixd not defined", procName, 1); 750 751 if (pixSizesEqual(pixs, pixd)) /* nothing to do */ 752 return 0; 753 754 /* Make sure we can copy the data */ 755 pixGetDimensions(pixs, &w, &h, &d); 756 wpl = pixGetWpl(pixs); 757 bytes = 4 * wpl * h; 758 if ((data = (l_uint32 *)pix_malloc(bytes)) == NULL) 759 return ERROR_INT("pix_malloc fail for data", procName, 1); 760 761 /* OK, do it */ 762 pixSetWidth(pixd, w); 763 pixSetHeight(pixd, h); 764 pixSetDepth(pixd, d); 765 pixSetWpl(pixd, wpl); 766 pixFreeData(pixd); /* free any existing image data */ 767 pixSetData(pixd, data); /* set the uninitialized memory buffer */ 768 pixCopyResolution(pixd, pixs); 769 return 0; 770 } 771 772 773 /*! 774 * \brief pixCopyColormap() 775 * 776 * \param[in] pixd 777 * \param[in] pixs copies the colormap to %pixd 778 * \return 0 if OK, 1 on error 779 * 780 * 
   781   * Notes:
   782   *      (1) This destroys the colormap in pixd, unless the operation is a no-op
   783   *
784 */ 785 l_ok 786 pixCopyColormap(PIX *pixd, 787 const PIX *pixs) 788 { 789 l_int32 valid; 790 const PIXCMAP *cmaps; 791 PIXCMAP *cmapd; 792 793 PROCNAME("pixCopyColormap"); 794 795 if (!pixs) 796 return ERROR_INT("pixs not defined", procName, 1); 797 if (!pixd) 798 return ERROR_INT("pixd not defined", procName, 1); 799 if (pixs == pixd) 800 return 0; /* no-op */ 801 802 pixDestroyColormap(pixd); 803 if ((cmaps = pixs->colormap) == NULL) /* not an error */ 804 return 0; 805 pixcmapIsValid(cmaps, &valid); 806 if (!valid) 807 return ERROR_INT("cmap not valid", procName, 1); 808 809 if ((cmapd = pixcmapCopy(cmaps)) == NULL) 810 return ERROR_INT("cmapd not made", procName, 1); 811 pixSetColormap(pixd, cmapd); 812 return 0; 813 } 814 815 816 /*! 817 * \brief pixSizesEqual() 818 * 819 * \param[in] pix1, pix2 820 * \return 1 if the two pix have same {h, w, d}; 0 otherwise. 821 */ 822 l_int32 823 pixSizesEqual(const PIX *pix1, 824 const PIX *pix2) 825 { 826 PROCNAME("pixSizesEqual"); 827 828 if (!pix1 || !pix2) 829 return ERROR_INT("pix1 and pix2 not both defined", procName, 0); 830 80 * l_int32 pixcmapWriteStream() 81 * l_int32 pixcmapWriteMem() 82 * 83 * Extract colormap arrays and serialization 84 * l_int32 pixcmapToArrays() 85 * l_int32 pixcmapToRGBTable() 86 * l_int32 pixcmapSerializeToMemory() 87 * PIXCMAP *pixcmapDeserializeFromMemory() 88 * char *pixcmapConvertToHex() 89 * 90 * Colormap transforms 91 * l_int32 pixcmapGammaTRC() 92 * l_int32 pixcmapContrastTRC() 93 * l_int32 pixcmapShiftIntensity() 94 * l_int32 pixcmapShiftByComponent() 95 * 96 * Note: 97 * (1) colormaps in leptonica have a maximum of 256 entries. 98 * (2) nalloc, the allocated size of the palette array, is related 99 * to the depth d of the pixels by: 100 * nalloc = 2^(d) 101 * 102 * 103 */ 104 105 #ifdef HAVE_CONFIG_H 106 #include 107 #endif /* HAVE_CONFIG_H */ 108 109 #include 110 #include "allheaders.h" 111 112 /*-------------------------------------------------------------* 113 * Colormap creation and addition * 114 *-------------------------------------------------------------*/ 115 /*! 116 * \brief pixcmapCreate() 117 * 118 * \param[in] depth of pix, in bpp 119 * \return cmap, or NULL on error 120 */ 121 PIXCMAP * 122 pixcmapCreate(l_int32 depth) 123 { 124 RGBA_QUAD *cta; 125 PIXCMAP *cmap; 126 127 PROCNAME("pixcmapCreate"); 128 129 if (depth != 1 && depth != 2 && depth !=4 && depth != 8) 130 return (PIXCMAP *)ERROR_PTR("depth not in {1,2,4,8}", procName, NULL); 131 132 cmap = (PIXCMAP *)LEPT_CALLOC(1, sizeof(PIXCMAP)); 133 cmap->depth = depth; 134 cmap->nalloc = 1 << depth; 135 cta = (RGBA_QUAD *)LEPT_CALLOC(cmap->nalloc, sizeof(RGBA_QUAD)); 136 cmap->array = cta; 137 cmap->n = 0; 138 return cmap; 139 } 140 141 142 /*! 143 * \brief pixcmapCreateRandom() 144 * 145 * \param[in] depth of pix, in bpp: 2, 4 or 8 146 * \param[in] hasblack 1 if the first color is black; 0 if no black 147 * \param[in] haswhite 1 if the last color is white; 0 if no white 148 * \return cmap, or NULL on error 149 * 150 * 
   151   * Notes:
   152   *      (1) This sets up a colormap with random colors,
   153   *          where the first color is optionally black, the last color
   154   *          is optionally white, and the remaining colors are
   155   *          chosen randomly.
   156   *      (2) The number of randomly chosen colors is:
   157   *               2^(depth) - haswhite - hasblack
   158   *      (3) Because rand() is seeded, it might disrupt otherwise
   159   *          deterministic results if also used elsewhere in a program.
   160   *      (4) rand() is not threadsafe, and will generate garbage if run
   161   *          on multiple threads at once -- though garbage is generally
   162   *          what you want from a random number generator!
   163   *      (5) Modern rand()s have equal randomness in low and high order
   164   *          bits, but older ones don't.  Here, we're just using rand()
   165   *          to choose colors for output.
   166   *
167 */ 168 PIXCMAP * 169 pixcmapCreateRandom(l_int32 depth, 170 l_int32 hasblack, 171 l_int32 haswhite) 172 { 173 l_int32 ncolors, i; 174 l_int32 red[256], green[256], blue[256]; 175 PIXCMAP *cmap; 176 177 PROCNAME("pixcmapCreateRandom"); 178 179 if (depth != 2 && depth != 4 && depth != 8) 180 return (PIXCMAP *)ERROR_PTR("depth not in {2, 4, 8}", procName, NULL);
